- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >3% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward; delay or dampen the correction to allow for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward more aggressively.
- Model tends to lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns from negative to positive; add a small lagged adjustment to forecast.
- In the 30-day horizon, model often underestimates upward momentum in volatile periods; increase forecast slightly if sentiment is bullish and price is trending.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to prioritize recent sentiment signals.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 2-3 consecutive days of price reversal), model may overfit to recent trend; apply a dampening factor to avoid overcorrection.
